subject: Brighton Bank DPA — initial counsel comments and eSign plan
messages:
From: Lisa Hart <lisa.hart@brightonbank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paul Owens <paul.owens@brightonbanklegal.com>
Date: 2028-09-12 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Brighton Bank - initial DPA and counsel notes

Connor —

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Our privacy team has taken a first pass and attached annotated comments (Brighton_DPA_Round1_comments.pdf). High level items we need you to confirm before counsel will sign off:

- Transfers: Brighton requires explicit wording on EU->US transfers; counsel wants either SCCs + EU-US addendum or an explicit transfer mechanism clause.
- Subprocessors: we need a more granular notice timeline (current clause says 30 days; legal prefers 60 and an explicit right to object within 30 days of notice).
- Audit & logs: retention period needs clarity — Brighton's baseline is 7 years for audit logs supporting financial investigations. Please confirm whether Redwood can commit to that retention or offer an export option.
- Security: KMS/HSM attestations — counsel asks for the key management options to be made explicit in Annex B.

Can we get responses to each item and a proposed esign route (DocuSign preferred) by EOD Friday? We have a procurement milestone next week.

Attachments: Brighton_DPA_Round1_comments.pdf (annotated), procurement_checklist.xlsx (ref)

—Lisa
Lisa Hart
Head of Vendor Risk & Procurement
Brighton Bank

Subject: RE: Brighton Bank - initial DPA and counsel notes

Lisa —

Appreciate the quick review and the annotated file. I've uploaded the comments to our shared drive and pulled together the internal owners. Quick answers up front, we will: 

- Transfers: propose SCCs + an EU-US transfer addendum (we'll draft language and include a fallback routing policy).
- Subprocessors: okay to extend notice to 60 days; we'll propose an explicit 30-day objection period in the notice flow and include the subprocessor inventory as an annex.
- Audit & logs: Redwood can retain audit logs for up to 7 years for enterprise contracts with the appropriate data handling caveats; if Brighton prefers not to keep us as the retention authority we can provide an export/transfer process.
- KMS/HSM: we'll add a short Annex B outlining KMS options (customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM or Redwood-managed with FIPS 140-2 attestation).

Next steps: Neha, can you coordinate a single document with the proposed redlines for Brighton's counsel to review? Marissa — please attach the subprocessor inventory (latest). I'll propose DocuSign unless Brighton indicates a preferred vendor.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Paul Owens <paul.owens@brightonbanklegal.com>

Date: 2028-09-13 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Brighton Bank - initial DPA and counsel notes

Connor/Neha —

Thanks. A couple of clarifying points from legal after reviewing your bullets:

1) SCCs + Addendum: acceptable, but Brighton needs an explicit escalation path if a transfer is blocked (e.g., data localization requirement triggers). Please identify which model clauses you're adopting and confirm whether Redwood will support EU SCCs 2021 or the latest adopted text.

2) Subprocessor notice: the 60/30 split is acceptable in principle but counsel asks for a process diagram in the annex showing notice timelines and objection mechanics.

3) Audit logs retention: counsel will accept a contractual export mechanism provided: (a) logs are maintained in searchable format for 7 years, and (b) Brighton has a right to request a certified export within 30 days of termination.

4) Security Annex: need concrete language around key custody and proof points (certs, SOC2 include but not limited to KMS attestations). A short template Annex B we can review would speed sign-off.

Please route a consolidated redline (single document) and we will review and come back with an actionable list.

Regards,
Paul Owens
Associate — Legal Operations
Brighton Bank Legal
